config.title: Intro to Computer Science
config.description: Fundamental CS concepts: data types, algorithms, memory, and computation theory.

questions.question: Which data type is used to store a single character in most programming languages?
questions.explanation: char (short for character) is the data type designed to hold a single character value such as 'a' or '3'.

questions.question: A boolean data type can store three possible values: true, false, and null.
questions.hint: What does the 'bi' in boolean mean?
questions.explanation: Boolean is a binary data type — it can only hold one of two values: true or false. Null is a separate concept representing 'no value'.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of an algorithm?

options.label: A
options.text: It always produces the fastest possible solution

options.label: B
options.text: It is a finite sequence of well-defined instructions

options.label: C
options.text: It must be written in a programming language

options.label: D
options.text: It requires a graphical user interface

questions.hint: Think about what makes a recipe distinct from random cooking.
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a finite sequence of precise, unambiguous instructions that solve a problem. It need not be optimal, coded, or visual — just clear and complete.

questions.question: Which type of memory loses its contents when the computer is powered off?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile — it requires power to retain data. ROM, hard drives, and SSDs are non-volatile and retain data without power.

questions.question: O(n) means the algorithm runs in constant time regardless of input size.
questions.hint: The 'n' in O(n) stands for the size of the input.
questions.explanation: O(n) describes linear time — the runtime grows proportionally with the input size. O(1) is constant time, which remains unchanged regardless of input size.

questions.question: A compiler translates source code into machine code:

options.label: C
options.text: Only when a runtime error occurs

questions.explanation: A compiler translates the entire source program into machine code (or an intermediate form) in one pass before execution begins. An interpreter translates and executes line by line.

questions.question: A pointer stores:

options.label: B
options.text: The memory address of another variable

options.label: C
options.text: The data type of a variable

options.label: D
options.text: The size of a data type

questions.explanation: A pointer is a variable whose value is the memory address of another variable. It does not store the data itself — it stores the location where the data can be found.

questions.question: A high-level language like Python generally runs faster than a low-level language like C because it is more abstract.
questions.hint: What does 'closer to the hardware' imply about speed?
questions.explanation: Lower-level languages like C give programmers fine-grained control over memory and CPU, resulting in faster execution. Python's high-level abstractions add overhead, making it generally slower.

questions.question: Binary search requires which condition to work correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: The data is stored in a linked list

options.label: C
options.text: The data has at most 100 elements

questions.hint: Think about how you'd find a word in a dictionary.
questions.explanation: Binary search repeatedly divides the search space in half. This only works correctly on sorted data, because it relies on comparing the target to the middle element to determine which half to search next.

questions.question: What happens when a program tries to access memory at an invalid address?

options.label: A
options.text: The program continues with a warning

options.label: B
options.text: The program crashes with a segmentation fault

options.label: C
options.text: The OS silently ignores the access

questions.explanation: Accessing an invalid memory address triggers a segmentation fault — the OS detects the violation of memory protection and forcibly terminates the program to prevent corruption.

questions.question: The Halting Problem is solvable for all general-purpose programming languages.
questions.hint: Think about Alan Turing's most famous proof.
questions.explanation: Turing proved the Halting Problem is undecidable — no general algorithm can determine whether an arbitrary program will halt or run forever. It is a fundamental limit of computation.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of quicksort?
questions.hint: Consider what happens when the pivot selection is consistently poor.
questions.explanation: Quicksort has O(n²) worst-case time complexity, occurring when poor pivot choices (e.g., always picking smallest or largest) create highly unbalanced partitions. Good pivot selection mitigates this.

questions.question: What is a memory leak?

options.label: A
options.text: When a program reads from an invalid memory address

options.label: B
options.text: When allocated memory is never freed and accumulates over time

options.label: C
options.text: When two threads access the same memory simultaneously

options.label: D
options.text: When the stack overflows due to deep recursion

questions.hint: Memory is allocated but the reference to it is lost.
questions.explanation: A memory leak occurs when a program allocates heap memory but loses all references to it without freeing it. Over time this exhausts available memory, degrading or crashing the program.

flashcards.definition: A finite, ordered set of instructions that solves a problem or performs a computation.

Linear time — the algorithm's run time grows proportionally with the size of the input.

algorithms.definition: A step-by-step procedure for solving a problem in a finite number of steps.
A mathematical notation describing the limiting behavior of an algorithm's complexity.

computation-theory.definition: Translates source code into machine code before execution.
The problem of determining whether a given program will finish running or continue forever.

memory.definition: Volatile memory used by the CPU to store actively used data.
A variable holding the memory address of another variable.
When allocated memory is never freed and accumulates over time.

data-types.definition: A data type with exactly two values: true and false.
A data type that stores a single alphanumeric character.
